title: About ME
text:
I am a Master of Data Science student at the University of British Columbia with a background in Applied Mathematics and experience in statistics, programming, and quantitative analysis.
My academic background includes research in biomathematics, where I worked on mathematical models to study biological systems and explored how quantitative methods can be used to understand complex real-world processes. This experience strengthened my interest in modelling, data analysis, and research-driven problem solving.
I also participated in AI4Good, where I worked on an applied machine learning project focused on developing an assistive image-classification system. That experience gave me hands-on exposure to the challenges of working with real-world data, model development, evaluation, and communicating the limitations and practical impact of AI systems.
Through the MDS program, I am continuing to strengthen my skills in Python, R, machine learning, statistical modelling, data visualization, and data communication. My goal is to build a career in data science where I can combine my mathematical background, research experience, and interest in machine learning to solve meaningful problems.

title: My first weeks in MDS
section: My First Week of MDS: A New Chapter Begins
text:
My First Week of MDS: A New Chapter Begins
There are some moments in life that feel both exciting and overwhelming at the same time. Starting my MDS was one of those moments.
My first week of MDS has been a mix of new experiences, new people, unfamiliar routines, and a lot of thoughts about what lies ahead. After working toward this next step for so long, actually being here feels a little surreal.

title: My first weeks in MDS
text:
The First Day
Walking into university on the first day, I had so many emotions running through my mind. I was excited to begin this new chapter, but I was also nervous. Everything felt new—the surroundings, the people, the classrooms, and even the feeling of being a postgraduate student.
There was also a quiet realization that this wasn’t just another academic milestone. MDS is a serious commitment, and I knew that the next few years would challenge me in ways I hadn’t experienced before.

title: My first weeks in MDS
text:
Meeting New People
One of the best parts of the first week was meeting my batchmates and getting to know the people I’ll be spending the next few years with.
At first, everyone seemed a little reserved and unsure, probably because we were all trying to find our place. Slowly, conversations started happening, introductions turned into jokes, and unfamiliar faces began to feel a little more familiar.
It’s comforting to realize that everyone is experiencing some version of the same nervousness and excitement.

title: My first weeks in MDS
text:
Getting Used to the Routine
The first week also meant trying to understand a completely new routine.
There was a lot to take in—classes, departments, faculty, clinical responsibilities, schedules, and countless little things that you don’t really think about until you’re actually there.
I’m slowly learning that MDS isn’t just about studying harder. It’s also about managing time, staying organized, being responsible, and learning how to balance academics with everything else.

title: My first weeks in MDS
text:
The Reality of MDS
Perhaps the biggest realization of my first week is that MDS is going to push me out of my comfort zone.
There will be days when everything goes well and days when I question whether I can keep up. There will be new skills to learn, mistakes to make, difficult cases to understand
